title: 2003 AMC 10A Problem 17
statement: The number of inches in the perimeter of an equilateral triangle equals the number of square inches in the area of its circumscribed circle. What is the radius, in inches, of the circle?

solutions.text:
Let the side length be \(s\) and the circumradius be \(R.\) From a \(30\)-\(60\)-\(90\) triangle formed by the center and a side, \(R = \dfrac{s}{\sqrt{3}},\) so \(s = R\sqrt{3}.\)

The perimeter is \(3s = 3R\sqrt{3}\) and the circle’s area is \(\pi R^2.\)

Setting them equal, \(3R\sqrt{3} = \pi R^2,\) so \(R = \dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{\pi}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: For an equilateral triangle of side \(s,\) the circumradius is \(R = \dfrac{s}{\sqrt{3}}\)
Set the perimeter \(3s\) equal to the area \(\pi R^2,\) then substitute \(s = R\sqrt{3}\)
